Oliver Whatmuff joined Stockport County on a season-long loan from Manchester City in July 2026.

The highly-rated goalkeeper came through Manchester City’s Academy after joining the club at the age of eight, signing his first professional contract in 2025. He has also represented England at youth level.

Whatmuff arrived at Edgeley Park following an impressive first season in senior football with Rochdale, where he worked under County manager Jimmy McNulty. He kept 18 clean sheets during their 2025/26 National League campaign and played a key role in helping the club win promotion back to the EFL.

The young goalkeeper produced a standout performance in the play-off final at Wembley, saving two penalties in the shootout victory over Boreham Wood.

He reunited with McNulty at County ahead of the 2026/27 League One season.

Exciting young goalkeeper Andrew Wogan joined County in July 2024, signing on a long-term contact from Irish side Drogheda United on a long-term contract.

Upon signing a four-year-deal, Andrew then returned to Drogheda on loan for the remiander of the Irish season, going on to win the FAI Cup with the Club in November - the first time Drogheda had won the competition since 2005.

The young shot stopper gained significant experience during his time in the Republic of Ireland, establishing himself as Drogheda’s number one goalkeeper at the age of just 17, making over 40 appearances for the club in all competitions - winning their Young Player of the Year award in 2023.

He has also featured seven times for Republic of Ireland U19s, and recently made his debut for Ireland U21s, keeping a clean sheet in a draw with Qatar.

Andrew has yet to make his County debut since moving to Edgeley Park, but enjoyed a successful loan spell at National League North side, Marine. Playing under former County boss Neil Young, the Irishman kept six clean sheets in ten league appearances, helping the side secure safety in the sixth tier with a run of seven wins in eight games. The goalkeeper's performances saw him recalled early from his loan spell, serving as Corey Addai's understudy during our promotion chase in League One.

Defender Josh Dacres-Cogley joined County in January 2026, signing from promotion rivals Bolton Wanderers for an undisclosed fee.

Josh departed Bolton after two and a half years at the Toughsheet Stadium, having made over 100 appearances for the Trotters and helping them to reach the League One Play-Off final in 2024.

Comfortable playing at right-back or right-wing-back, the 29-year-old began his career in Birmingham City’s academy, signing his first pro-contract with the Blues in 2015.

He made his senior debut for the Championship club a year later, playing the entire 120 minutes of a Carabao Cup tie against Oxford United. His first league appearance came just a few months later, starting and impressing in a 2-1 win against Brentford.

Following a productive loan spell at Crawley Town, Josh went on to join Tranmere Rovers on a free transfer in 2021.

It was at Prenton Park where the defender’s career really took off. Across his two seasons with Rovers, he appeared in 91 of their 92 league games – providing a constant threat down the right flank with two goals and eight assists.

That form earned him the move to Bolton, where he quickly became a first-team regular. He missed just two league games in his debut season as the Trotters finished in 3rd, before starting all three games in a play-off campaign that ultimately ended in defeat to Oxford United at Wembley.

Josh ended the season with three goals and six assists, with his performances earning him a place in the League One Team of the Season.

The 29-year-old signed an 18-month deal to move to Edgeley Park midway through the 25/26 campaign, making his Hatters debut in a 3-2 win against Rotherham United at Edgeley Park.

players.name: Ethan Pye

2026/27 SPONSORS

AWAY: Harry Corbett

Left-sided defender, Ethan joined County in July 2021 at the age of 18, shortly after being released by Rochdale AFC, where he had been part of their development squad.

He won the Youth Alliance League Cup during his time at Rochdale, with County seeing off competition from several other sides to secure the youngster’s services on a two-year-deal.

Ethan made his first-team debut for the club in October 2021, starting our National League game away at Weymouth and impressing at the back, in a 2-1 win for County.

He made a further two appearances against Dover and Bolton in the FA Cup, before spending the second half of the campaign on loan at Spennymoor Town in the National League North.

The defender returned to the North-East for the 2022/23 campaign, enjoying a brilliant season on loan at National League side Gateshead. He made 39 appearances during his time with The Heed, helping them to reach the FA Trophy final at Wembley before being named as the club’s Players’ Player of the Year.

He has returned to Edgeley Park in 2023 to become a key part of Dave Challinor’s first-team squad, playing 42 times during the 2023/24 campaign as we secured the League Two title - our first EFL championship in 57 years. The defender grabbed his first goal for the Club on the night we secured the title, heading home our final goal in a 5-2 win away at Notts County - putting the seal on one Stockport County's greatest ever nights. His form saw him rewarded with a new three-year deal that Summer.

Making the step up to League One the following season, Ethan continued to grow in maturity and stature, starting 42 of our 46 league games as we secured a third-place finish. The consistency of his performances on the left side of our defence made him undroppable for Dave Challinor's side, and his contribution saw him pick up the Club's Young Player, Supporters' Player and Players' Player of the Year Awards.

The experienced Irish centre-back began his senior career with Celtic, where he made his first-team debut after progressing through the club’s youth system. He later gained experience with Oldham Athletic, Cork City and Walsall before permanent spells with Bury, Rochdale and Charlton Athletic.

O’Connell joined Wrexham in January 2023 and became an important part of a side that secured three successive promotions, taking the club from the National League to the Championship. He made 84 league appearances during his time at the Racecourse Ground.

After leaving Wrexham, he spent the second half of the 2025/26 season with Barnsley, making 25 League One appearances and scoring once before making the move to County.

A commanding and experienced centre-back, O’Connell adds leadership, aerial strength and significant EFL experience to County’s defensive options.

Attacking full-back Tayo Edun joined County on a free transfer from Peterborough United ahead of the 2025/26 season in League One.

The 27-year-old moved to Edgeley Park following a strong end to the 2024/25 campaign with The Posh, featuring 17 times for Darren Ferguson's side after joining them in Charlton in January.

Prior to that, Tayo began his career at Fulham, making his debut for The Cottagers at the age of 18, starting a Carabao Cup tie against Leyton Orient.

Tayo made seven appearances during his time at Craven Cottage before enjoying a loan spell at Championship side, Ipswich Town - scoring on his debut for the Tractor Boys in a 2-2 draw with his future side, Blackburn Rovers.

Upon leaving Fulham in 2020, Tayo made the move to Lincoln City - becoming a key figure in defence for Michael Appleton's promotion-chasing side. He appeared in 42 of Lincoln's 46 league games during the 2020/21 season as the Imps finished 5th, before losing the League One Play-Off Final to Blackpool at Wembley.

His impressive form at Sincil Bank saw him draw interest from Championship clubs the following season, eventually joining Blackburn Rovers on deadline day for an undisclosed fee.

The former England youth international made 28 appearances in the Championship during his two seasons at Ewood Park, before moving on to Charlton and then Peterborough.

Oldham-born Ryan joined the Club from Fleetwood in 2021, having made 13 appearances in League One for the Cod Army after coming through their academy.

Capable of playing anywhere down the left-hand side, Ryan made his professional debut for Fleetwood at the age of just 17, away against Southend United back in September 2018.

He made his full EFL debut for the side just a few months later against Walsall, impressing enough to retain his place in the side over the next three games and drawing high praise from then manager Joey Barton.

He spent the second part of the 2019/20 season on loan at Lancaster City, making six appearances and scoring one before their season was cut short due to the Covid pandemic.

He made a further seven first-team appearances for Fleetwood in the 2020/21 season before making the move to County.

Ryan made his debut for the Club in April 2021, coming on as a substitute in a 4-0 win away at King’s Lynn Town. He scored his first goal for County in September 2021, a late winner against promotion-rivals Wrexham at Edgeley Park.

Ryan’s form was something of a revelation following the appointment of manager Dave Challinor as he became a mainstay at left-wing-back, registering 14 assists in his 36 appearances in all competitions, winning the Club’s Young Player of the Year Award in our title winning season.

It was an award he would pick up again the following season after seamlessly making the step up into League Two, scoring three times and setting up another 11 in 32 appearances as County just missed out in the League Two play-off final.

An ACL injury picked up in training cruely cut his 2024/24 campaign short in September, forcing Ryan to watch on from the stands as County went on to secure the League Two title with two games to spare.

The defender made his long-awaited return to fitness during the 2024/25 season, playing 22 times for the Club in all competitions and registering three assists. Ryan made his 100th appearance for the Club in March 2025, helping us keep a clean sheet in a 0-0 draw with Charlton Athletic at Edgeley Park.

A versatile, front-foot player capable of playing in midfield and in defence, the 24-year-old began his career in West Ham’s academy before going on to enjoy spells in League One with Charlton Athletic and Portsmouth.

A particularly impressive performance against County in April caught the eye, with County moving quickly to secure his services in preparation for their return to League One.

Defender Brad Hills joined County in a permanent deal in the summer of 2026, signing from Norwich City for a significant undisclosed fee following a successful loan spell at Edgeley Park.

Brad penned a five-year deal with the Hatters, having already established himself as one of the best defenders in League One during his time on loan with the club.

Originally joining in February 2025, the 21-year-old made 18 appearances in the second half of the campaign as County narrowly missed out on promotion to the Championship.

He won Man of the Match on his debut in a 2-1 win against Barnsley at Edgeley Park and went on to start all but two matches following his February arrival, scoring his first County goal in front of the Cheadle End during a 3-1 win against Rotherham United.

He quickly formed an effective partnership at the back alongside fellow youngster Ethan Pye, with the pair playing a key role as County finished the campaign with seven wins from their final eight league games.

Prior to his time in SK3, Brad also enjoyed a productive loan spell with Accrington Stanley in League Two – winning the Club’s Player of the Year award in a season that saw him feature 48 times for John Coleman’s side.

The Norfolk-born defender departed Norwich having made five appearances for the Canaries after coming through their academy, before committing his long-term future to the Hatters.

County captain Lewis Bate joined County in the Summer of 2024/25, signing a three-year deal at Edgeley Park shortly after his release from Championship outfit Leeds United.

A technically gifted midfielder who controls the game from deep, Lewis made the move to County with plenty of experience already under his belt at 21, having already featured in the Premier League, League One and League Two.

The former England Youth International began his career in Chelsea’s Cobham academy, spending ten years with the Blues. He was named in a matchday squad three times whilst at Stamford Bridge, under Frank Lampard and Thomas Tuchel, before joining Leeds United for a seven-figure fee.

Whilst at Elland Road, Lewis made his Premier League debut under Marcelo Bielsa, coming off the bench in a game against West Ham United.

The skipper then enjoyed a successful loan spell at Oxford United in League One, featuring 35 times for The Us and twice winning the Club’s Player of the Month award, before a hand injury cut his season short.

With his game time at Elland Road limited, Lewis spent the second half of the 2023/24 season on loan at promotion-chasing MK Dons in League Two and once again caught the eye, with Dave Challinor quick to bring him to Edgeley Park once his contract at Leeds expired.

Despite just arriving at the Club, Lewis was named as Club Captain ahead of the start of the 2024/25 season. He made his debut in our 2-0 win against Cambridge United on opening day and went on to play 37 times in is first season at Edgeley Park, scoring twice, as County narrowly missed out on promotion to the Championship via the play-offs.

players.name: Oliver Norwood
players.biography:
2026/27 SPONSORS

HOME: Penumbra Finance

AWAY: Swapp Family

Veteran midfielder Ollie Norwood was a statement signing for the Club in the Summer 2024, joining shortly after the Club’s promotion to League One as Champions.

The 34-year-old had spent the previous campaign playing in the Premier League for Sheffield United, featuring 27 times, but following his release from Bramhall Lane opted to sign a three-year-deal at Edgeley Park.

Norwood is widely regarded as a Club legend for the Blades, captaining the side across his six seasons at Bramhall Lane and twice winning promotion to the top flight with the club.

A former Northern Ireland international and serial winner, Ollie has a wealth of experience from a playing career spent at the top level of the game during spells with Brighton, Fulham and Sheffield United.

He began his career in Manchester United's academy, gaining first-team experience in League One and the Championship through loan spells at Carlisle United, Scunthorpe United and Coventry City.

In 2012, he turned down new terms at Old Trafford to pursue first-team football, going on to join Huddersfield Town in the Championship. He spent two years in Yorkshire, before going on to enjoy spells at Reading and Brighton & Hove Albion.

The midfielder was a key figure as Brighton secured promotion to the Premier League for the first time under Chris Hughton, playing 33 times in the league. The following year, he joined Fulham on loan for the campaign and again secured promotion from the Championship, this time via the play-offs, with Ollie coming off the bench at Wembley as Fulham defeated Aston Villa 1-0 in the showpiece final.

Ahead of the 2018/19 campaign he moved to Sheffield United, initially on a loan deal that was made permanent just six months later. Remarkably, he then went on to enjoy a third successive Championship promotion that season, as the Blades finished runners up under Chris Wilder. Ollie played 43 times in the Championship that season, earning a place in the PFA Championship Team of the Year for the role he played.

At 28, and after three promotions, the midfielder was finally given his opportunity to play in the Premier League and excelled, featuring in all 38 of Sheffield United's league games as they finished 9th in the top flight, falling just short of the European places.

Although the Blades lost their place in the Premier League in 2020, Norwood remained a key figure at Bramall Lane and he was again ever-present in the Championship as they won promotion back to the top division in 2022.

Upon moving to Edgeley Park at the age of 33, the midfielder has shown no signs of slowing down. Making his debut in our 2-0 win against Bristol Rovers in August, he went on to play 49 times in his first season with the Club, scoring five goals. His performances at the back end of the season were crucial as County recorded a 3rd place finish in League One – our highest league position in 23 years.

A versatile and creative attacking midfielder, Wood can operate in a number of roles and adds goals, technical quality and further attacking options to Jimmy McNulty’s squad.

The Scotland U21 international took part in pre-season training with the rest of the first-team yesterday, after signing a three-year-deal with the club option of an additional year at Edgeley Park.

The talented attacking midfielder had been at Manchester City since the age of six and brings plenty of experience from successful loan spells overseas and in the EFL.

The 22-year-old signed a five-year contract with City in 2021 following an impressive season in the Eerste Divisie with NAC Breda, where he scored six and assisted five in 36 appearances for the Dutch club, who narrowly missed out on promotion that year.

He then went on to join Lincoln City in League One, playing 44 times under manager Michael Appleton and scoring a further six goals before following Appleton to Blackpool in the Championship the following season.

Having returned to City last Summer to undergo surgery, Fiorini then moved Charlton Athletic on loan in January where he linked up with Appleton for the third time in three seasons. On this occasion, however, the reunion proved short-lived with Appleton leaving the club just a few weeks after the Lewis completed his move to the Valley.

Whilst he represented England at Under 15s level alongside the likes of Jude Bellingham, Jamal Musiala and Cole Palmer, the technically gifted midfielder has since chosen to represent Scotland – featuring ten times for their U21s side, whilst he has previously spent time training with the senior side under Steve Clarke.

At just 22, we are delighted to have signed Lewis on a long-term contact and look forward to seeing him develop further during his time at Edgeley Park.

Versatile midfielder Ben Osborn is currently on a season-long loan deal from Championship outfit Derby County.

The 31-year-old signed for County on deadline day, bringing a wealth of experience with him from a playing career that has seen him make over 350 appearances across the Premier League and the Championship.

Also capable of playing at left-back or left wing-back, the former England Youth International began his professional career at Nottingham Forest, joining their academy from rivals Derby County at the age of nine.

He rose through the ranks at the City Ground, winning the Club’s Academy Player of the Year award in 2012 before making his first-team debut for the Reds in March 2014, starting a 1-1 draw with Ipswich Town in the Championship.

He signed a five-year deal at Forest that summer, and went on to become a first-team regular the following season under Stuart Pearce.

Ben went on to enjoy six successful years at Forest – including a two-year spell where he didn’t miss a single league game in the Championship. His performances in the 2017/18 season saw him named as the Club’s Player of the Year, after scoring three times in 50 appearances in all competitions.

In 2019, Ben moved on to join Sheffield United for an undisclosed fee, following the Club’s promotion to the Premier League under Chris Wilder.

He made 13 appearances in the top-flight in his first season at Bramall Lane as the Blades finished 9th, narrowly missing out on a European place. He showed his quality in the second half of the season, playing a role in big wins against the likes of Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Wolverhampton Wanderers.

He became a key figure for the Blades whilst back in the second tier, helping them finish in a play-off spot in 2022, where they were beaten by former club Forest on penalties, before winning promotion back to the Premier League 12 months later.

He eventually departed Bramall Lane in 2024 after five years with the Blades, racking up 134 appearances – 61 of which came at the highest level in the English game.

He returned to his boyhood club Derby County, joining the Rams in 2024 on a two-year deal. He played 25 times in the Championship last season, helping the newly promoted club retain their place in the second tier.

He made his County debut in our league fixture away at Plymouth Argyle in September, and scored his first goal for the Hatters in our 2-0 win away at Doncaster Rovers in December.

players.name: Jack Diamond

AWAY: Lloyd & John Nelson

Former Sunderland winger Jack Diamond joined County on a three-year-deal in the Summer of 2024, shortly after the Club’s promotion to League One.

The exciting inside-forward spent ten years at the Stadium of Light prior to his move to Edgeley Park, having come through the academy for the Black Cats.

After making his senior first-team debut for Sunderland at 18 in the EFL Trophy, Diamond's first real taste of first-team football came on loan at Harrogate Town, making 31 appearances for the Yorkshire side as they secured promotion to the Football League in 2020.

In the play-off final against Notts County, he cemented his place in Harrogate folklore after scoring his side's third goal at Wembley, to secure their place in League Two for the very first time.

He then returned to Sunderland that Summer following the club’s relegation to League One, making 35 appearances for the North-East side as they narrowly missed out on promotion, losing to Lincoln City in the play-off semi-final. He did, however, go on to lift the EFL Trophy with the Club, coming off the bench as Sunderland beat Tranmere at Wembley.

Having re-joined Harrogate on loan the following season, Diamond would go on to enjoy the best year of his career to date in League Two, scoring 14 times and providing ten assists to be named as the club's Players' Player of the Year.

He followed that up with a further eight goals whilst on loan at Lincoln City in 2022/23, including a stunning first career hat-trick in a 6-3 win away at Bristol Rovers. His performances during his time with the Imps saw him nominated for the League One Player of the Month award in September 2022.

After a period of absence away from football due to personal circumstances, Jack returned to first-team action in January 2024, joining Carlisle United on loan.

Following the expiration of his contract at Sunderland, Jack made the move to Edgeley Park – making his debut for the Club in a 2-0 win against Cambridge United in League One. Jack’s first goal for the Club came in September 2024, grabbing a consolation in a defeat to Leyton Orient in SK3.

In his first season with the Club, Jack made 40 appearances in all competitions. In that time, he helped himself to five goals and five assists, finishing the season strongly and picking up the Club’s Player of the Month award for April.

Icelandic goal machine Benony Breki Andresson joined County in January 2025, signed for an undisclosed fee from Icelandic top-flight side KR as part of the Club’s Emerging Talents Programme.

The teenage sensation caught the eye after breaking all the goalscoring records in his native country, scoring 21 times in just 26 league appearances in 2024 – a new Icelandic top-flight record, achieved at the age of 19.

A prolific goalscorer at youth level, the Iceland U21 international spent two years in Italy with Serie A side Bologna before returning home to sign for KR in 2023. He scored nine league goals in his first season with the Club before that record-breaking year, with a five-goal haul against HK on the final day of the campaign seeing him beat the previous record of 19 goals.

Despite expectation being that Beno would be a signing for the future at Edgeley Park, his performances in training meant he was soon involved with Dave Challinor’s first-team, making his debut for the Club as a substitute in our FA Cup tie against Crystal Palace.

He soon announced himself to the Edgeley Park faithful in some style, coming off the bench at half-time in a game against Blackpool with the Hatters trailing 1-0 at the time. Within a couple of minutes, he slotted home his first goal for the Club, before heading home the winner at the Cheadle End nine minutes from time.

As if to prove that was no fluke, just a few days later he was at it again – coming off the bench late on to score a deft late header against Northampton Town to earn County a point on the road.

In total he made 13 appearances in the second half of the 2024/25 season, scoring four times, with manager Dave Challinor describing the Ice Man as the best finisher at the Club.

Glover joined Barnet in 2024 and enjoyed two impressive seasons with the Bees. He helped the club win the National League title in his first campaign before establishing himself in League Two, and was named Barnet’s Player of the Year in both seasons at the club.

The big man.

Striker, Kyle Wootton joined County in the Summer of 2022, becoming the Club’s first signing following promotion back to the Football League after a 12-year absence.

The forward signed on a free transfer from Notts County after three seasons at Meadow Lane, during which time he scored 59 goals in just 134 appearances for the Club, establishing himself as one of the best forwards in the National League. Prior to that, the forward had spent six seasons with Scunthorpe United.

Kyle made his debut for County against Barrow on the opening day of the 2022/23 season, and scored his first goal for the Club a few weeks later in a 1-0 win over Colchester United.

He quickly became a favourite at Edgeley Park, finishing our first season back in the EFL as our top scorer with 14 goals and winning the Club’s Player and Players’ Player of the Year awards despite injury cutting his campaign short in April.

Returning from that injury in October, the big man added a further 12 goals in 37 appearances during the 2023/24 season as County were crowned Champions of League Two – the first promotion of Kyle’s career.

Back in League One for the first time since his Scunthorpe days, Wootts enjoyed a fine start to the 2024/25 season with three goals and two assists in his first four appearances. Shortly after, the big man penned a new three-year deal with the Club.

Kyle featured 52 times over the course of the campaign, more than any other County player, and contributed 13 goals and eight assists in that time. His 21 goal contributions was also the most of any player in the Hatters squad, helping us to a 3rd place finish in League One.

AWAY: Charlotte & Hannah Brown

Gambia international striker Adama Sidibeh joined County in January 2026, signing from Scottish side St Johnstone for an undisclosed fee.

The move capped a remarkable career rise for Adama, who just three years prior was scoring goals for fun down the road at Cheadle Heath Nomads in non-league.

The pacy and powerful forward began his playing career in his native Gambia, featuring for Marimoo and Gambia Ports Authority, before moving to England in 2022 to reunite with his family.

After arriving in England, Adama enjoyed a short spell at AFC Blackpool before signing for Cheadle Heath Nomads in December 2022.

He spent just six months with Nomads but made a big impression in his short time there, scoring 20 times in the second half of the 2022/23 season and winning the club’s Player of the Year award.

That form earned him a move up a division as he signed for Warrington Rylands, where he again scored freely – finding the net 16 times in 30 appearances in the first half of the campaign.

With his goalscoring exploits inevitably drawing interest from the EFL and from clubs north of the border, Adama was soon on the move again - with Scottish Premiership side St Johnstone signing him in January for an undisclosed fee.

His time in Scotland was a success, becoming a key player for The Saints during his two years at McDiarmid Park – departing with the club sat top of the Scottish Championship.

His performances in Scotland have also seen him become a regular for the Gambia national team, where he again made an immediate impact.

He made his debut for the Scorpions in a World Cup Qualifier against Seychelles, coming off the bench to score in a 5-1 win for Gambia. He went on to score seven times in his first nine appearances for his country – including back-to-back braces against Gabon and Seychelles again during the October 2025 international break.

Adama made his County debut as a substitute in our 2-1 win away at Blackpool in League One, before scoring his first goals for the club with a brace in our 4-0 EFL Trophy win at Port Vale.
